hook.text: The Netherlands moves 27% of all trips by bicycle. The secret is infrastructure.

buildup.text: Separated cycle tracks keep bikes away from cars — physical barriers, not just paint.

discovery.text: Protected intersections give cyclists their own signal phase and turning lanes.

twist.text: Paint-only bike lanes have crash rates five times higher than separated facilities.

climax.text: Copenhagen's Cykelslangen is a cycling bridge — elevated, heated, and snowplowed.

punchline.text: Build it safe and people will ride. Paint alone isn't enough.

quiz.question: Why are separated cycle tracks safer than painted bike lanes?
options: Cyclists travel faster on separated tracks due to better pavement
Physical barriers prevent vehicle intrusion, reducing crash rates significantly
Separated tracks are only used in areas with no car traffic
